passage:
Note to file, written the evening of the accident.

I reached the crossing from the market and found about a dozen people standing at the kerb, most with phones held up. Preeti, a first-year student, was one of them, filming. The delivery rider lay beside the kerb with one arm over the face. A shopkeeper told me it had been about six minutes and, as far as anyone knew, no call had been made; each person had assumed another had done it. I dialled 112. The ambulance arrived soon after.

Afterwards Preeti stood still with the phone still in hand and said, "I kept thinking someone else would do it." I sat with Preeti on the step and did not lecture. I asked what the video was for, and Preeti had no answer. I will invite Preeti to the next first-aid session.

Abhinav, hostel warden

qa.q: How long had the rider been on the road before anyone called for help?
qa.a: It had been about six minutes when the shopkeeper told the writer, and no call had been made.

qa.q: What was Preeti feeling as the ambulance left?
qa.a: Preeti seemed stunned and regretful, standing still with the phone in hand and admitting to thinking someone else would make the call.

qa.q: What could Preeti do differently next time, and why?
qa.a: Preeti could put the phone down and dial the emergency number straight away, or point at one person and ask them to call, because when everyone assumes someone else has called, no one does.

qa.q: How might the rider have experienced those minutes?
qa.a: The rider probably felt frightened and alone on the ground while people nearby only watched and waited.

grounding: Illustrates a person freezing and filming a crash while the injured rider waits and nobody calls for help for several minutes.

passage:
Monday, late.
I can't stop thinking about today. A cyclist got hit by a delivery van outside the metro station. He was lying there, holding his leg, and about ten of us were standing around. I took my phone out and started filming. I don't even know why. It's what I do when something happens.
Sahil was next to me, also filming. We all were. Nobody called anyone. I kept thinking someone else must have.
Then a tea-stall owner came running, shouted "Has anyone called?" and phoned 112 himself. It had been five or six minutes. The cyclist had been lying on the road that whole time, and I had a perfectly good phone in my hand.
The ambulance came. I deleted the video on the way home.
I feel sick about it. Next time I call first. I'm Lalit, and I'm writing that down so I remember.

qa.q: How does Lalit feel about having filmed the cyclist?
qa.a: Lalit feels sick with guilt and shame, having held a working phone for minutes without calling for help.

qa.q: What should Lalit do differently next time, and why?
qa.a: Lalit should call 112 or check that someone clearly has, because when everyone assumes someone else called, no one does.

qa.q: How might the cyclist have experienced those five or six minutes?
qa.a: The cyclist was likely in pain and frightened, surrounded by people with phones pointed at him but no help coming.

grounding: Shows a bystander filming a crash out of shock and habit while nobody calls for help for several minutes, delaying care.

Madhuri: did you see the video in the group? the accident near the college gate
Chandrika: yes. I took it
Madhuri: you were there?? was the girl okay?
Chandrika: I don't know. she was on the ground near her scooter. a car had hit her side
Madhuri: who called the ambulance?
Chandrika: I don't know. I just started filming and so did everyone
Madhuri: Chandrika it's four minutes long. nobody's helping her in the whole video
Chandrika: I know. I watched it again. you can hear someone say 'someone call' and then nothing
Madhuri: did the ambulance come?
Chandrika: the college guard called when he walked out. then it came
Madhuri: please delete it from the group. she wouldn't want that out there
Chandrika: deleting it now. I feel awful. I just froze and my hand did the filming

qa.a: Chandrika feels awful and ashamed, saying the freeze left only a hand filming while nobody helped.

qa.q: What should Chandrika have done instead of filming?
qa.a: Chandrika should have called 112 or checked clearly that someone had, since everyone filming meant no one called.

qa.q: How might the injured girl feel if she saw the video?
qa.a: She would likely feel hurt and exposed seeing herself on the ground for four minutes with people filming instead of helping.
